text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Slovenian newspapers:
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan started a three-day visit to Rome and the Vatican on Thursday.
- Threats on a Slovenian consulate and newspaper offices in Klagenfurt, Austria, by suspected rightist extremists are increasingly aggressive.
- Power of Slovenia's tax-offices will increase from the beginning of the next year, the Slovenian government said on Thursday.
- A bomb, thrown in the centre of Slovenia's second biggest town Maribor on Thursday night, caused minor damage and no injuries.

- Official results of Sunday's electoral referendum showed that turnout was just 37.94 percent of the country's 1.5 million electorate. The referendum failed to bring any changes to Slovenia's current electoral system.

- POP TV, Slovenia's most popular commercial televison broadcast over 5,900 hours of programmes in the first year of its existence. The station covers over 80 percent of Slovenia, the POP's management said on the first anniversary of the station.
- Tourism brought Slovenia profit of one billion U.S. dollars in the first 10 months of 1996, the country's officials said.
- Introducing the new chip identification cards for health insurance will be decided by parliament because of the cost of the project expected at 1.3 billion tolars ($9.3 million).
- Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will attend the European Union summit in Dublin on Saturday.
